sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Over 1400 killed in Gaza since October as Israeli strikes continue
cards.content: More than 1400 people in Gaza have been killed in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire started last October. The ceasefire was meant to end the war but Israel has kept launching strikes in Gaza almost every day. The total death toll is now over 74000. Israel says it's targeting Hamas operatives but the Gaza health ministry's figures are considered reliable by the UN.

cards.title: Three Sisters Drown Off Brighton Amid Rough Seas
cards.content: Three sisters Jane Christina and Rebecca who were all living in London took their own lives by drowning in the sea off Brighton. The coroner said they were living very private lives after their mother's death in 2010. The sisters visited the area where their mother died before going to Brighton where they drowned in rough sea conditions. Their father said it was heartbreaking to lose all three of his daughters.

cards.title: Former Ukrainian Officer Accuses Military Intelligence of Monaco Bomb Plot
cards.content: A former Ukrainian security officer Vitalii Zhykovych claims he believed a bomb attack in Monaco was ordered by senior members of Ukraine's military intelligence agency HUR. Zhykovych says he was a freelancer for the agency and had an agent Anastasia Berezovska who planted the bomb. He insists he did not send her to kill and did not kill her when her body was found with gunshot wounds. Zhykovych alleges that an active-duty intelligence officer from HUR Vladyslav Reut was behind the operation and communicated directly with Berezovska without Zhykovych's knowledge.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: South Korea develops rover with shape-shifting wheels for moon exploration
cards.content:
Here is a summary of the news article

South Korea is developing a rover with unique origami-inspired wheels that can change shape and adapt to the moon's surface. The wheels are made of flexible strips that interweave and can shrink to fit inside a lunar lander before expanding to navigate the moon's challenging terrain. The rover's developers hope to use it to explore the moon's lava tubes which could one day shelter human colonies. The team has tested the wheels in various environments including the moon's surface simulant and is now working on a self-driving rover using artificial intelligence.

cards.title: SpaceX buys wireless spectrum from Grain Management
cards.content: SpaceX the company founded by Elon Musk has agreed to buy a big chunk of wireless spectrum from a company called Grain Management. This spectrum will help SpaceX's Starlink service offer better coverage in the US. Starlink is a way for people to get internet access using satellites in space. The deal is still pending approval from the Federal Communications Commission.

cards.title: Nasdaq CEO Sees Tens of Billions in Locked Capital Unlocked with Tokenization
cards.content: Nasdaq CEO Adena Friedman believes that tokenization could unlock tens of billions of dollars in capital tied up in assets used as collateral globally. Tokenizing assets like Treasurys equities and money market funds along with the flow of money could make collateral more liquid. This process which uses blockchain technology has gained institutional interest over the past year particularly since the passage of the Genius Act in the US. Friedman also thinks that artificial intelligence could help financial institutions manage the shift to a 24/7 market.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: US Launches Vaccine Injury Study Program Amid Concerns Over Side Effects
cards.content: The US Department of Health and Human Services has launched a program to study and track vaccine injuries a long-standing priority for Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The program housed at the National Institutes of Health aims to understand who is vulnerable to vaccine injuries. Kennedy claims that federal scientists have ignored possible side effects including debunked theories linking immunizations to autism. This move has sparked concerns from public health advocates. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says the risk of vaccines causing serious reactions injuries or death is very remote.

cards.title: Beauty influencer's complex skincare routine raises concerns over unrealistic claims
cards.content: Greta Costioli a 29-year-old was once known for her "glass skin" on TikTok where she used a complex skincare routine with many products. She would apply seven layers of toner to achieve a smooth and pore-less complexion. This trend popularized by beauty influencers and celebrities has its roots in South Korean beauty culture. While some people may see positive results from these routines experts warn that they can be unrealistic and lead to skin problems like clogged pores irritation and breakouts.

cards.title: African pediatrician leads Union for International Cancer Control
cards.content: Dr. Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu a Nigerian pediatrician and cancer advocate has been elected president of the Union for International Cancer Control. She's the first African to lead the organization. Bagudu wants to focus on cancer care in low-income countries where cases and deaths are expected to rise sharply. She plans to use her position to bridge the gap between countries with limited cancer services and those with better resources. Bagudu wants to increase funding for cancer treatment and research improve access to diagnosis and treatment and reduce financial toxicity for patients. She also wants to prioritize prevention and focus on cancers that can be prevented or reduced through available interventions.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Maharashtra Declared Drought-Hit, Orders 10% Water Cut Amid Wastewater Crisis
cards.content: Almost 74% of Maharashtra a state in India was declared drought-hit in September after a very dry monsoon season. To manage water supplies the state has ordered local authorities to reduce water use by 10% from October 16. The state is also encouraging the reuse of treated wastewater for non-drinking purposes like gardening and construction. Currently only 57% of the state's wastewater is treated and just 17% is reused which is a problem because untreated wastewater is polluting rivers and lakes.

cards.title: India's species conservation efforts yield positive results globally.
cards.content: Wildlife populations worldwide have decreased by 73% over the past 50 years but India has seen an increase in several major species. According to a report by the World Wide Fund for Nature and the Zoological Society of London India has made progress in conserving species like tigers greater one-horned rhinoceroses and Asiatic lions. The report also notes that freshwater wildlife populations have experienced the steepest decline at 85% while marine populations have declined by 59%. India's conservation efforts have been successful with populations of these species increasing.

cards.title: Heavy Rain Hits North India, Snowfall Expected in Higher Himalayan Peaks
cards.content: Heavy rain hit Uttarakhand Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir with strong winds and snowfall expected on higher Himalayan peaks. Other areas like Kerala Tamil Nadu West Bengal and Sikkim are under alert for heavy rainfall thunderstorms lightning and gusty winds. In Delhi-NCR mornings and nights are cooler but days are still hot with isolated thunderstorms and showers possible. Punjab Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh might see thunderstorms lightning and strong winds prompting cautionary alerts. Meanwhile the southwest monsoon withdrawal is moving across India signaling changing weather patterns and the arrival of cooler conditions.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: EbonyLife Place Opens in London, Showcasing African Cinema and Culture
cards.content: A new cultural centre EbonyLife Place has opened in south-west London. It's a place where people can go to watch great movies learn about black and African cinema and enjoy food art and performances. The centre was founded by Mo Abudu a Nigerian media mogul and will show films from Nigeria and other African countries. It will also have masterclasses industry panels and live performances. The Mayor of London Lord Khan attended the opening and said that London is a great place for filming and that culture is important.

cards.title: BBC Announces Radio 4 Program Cuts to Save £500m
cards.content: The BBC has announced it will cut several Radio 4 programmes including You and Yours and Thinking Allowed to make £500m savings. The corporation will also reduce commissioning on Radio 5 Live and podcasts. Despite these cuts the BBC will invest in a new consumer programme and two new weekly shows exploring ideas and technology. Radio 4's flagship show In Our Time will expand in length while Start the Week and Farming Today will also grow.

cards.title: Wycombe Wanderers gets new anthem from indie-folk band Kingfishr
cards.content: A 16-year-old video game a music band and a football team unexpectedly came together. The indie-folk band Kingfishr wrote a song for Wycombe Wanderers a League One football team after adopting them in the video game Fifa 11. The song gained popularity on TikTok with over 190000 views and the band's lead singer Eddie Keogh attended a Wycombe Wanderers game was presented with a club shirt and even got to play the song over the stadium's speakers. The team and fans are excited about the new anthem and the band is welcome to return to the stadium anytime.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: UK watchdog investigates surge in "robo calls" amid suspected recruitment scam
cards.content: The UK's data watchdog the Information Commission's Office is investigating a big increase in complaints about "robo calls" that are suspected to be part of a recruitment scam. These calls ask you to add the caller to WhatsApp and the ICO thinks millions of people are getting these calls. They advise people to ignore calls from numbers they don't recognize and to block and report suspicious calls. The calls usually come from a UK mobile number but the ICO thinks the calls are actually coming from abroad.

cards.title: Asos Reports Data Breach, Hackers Access User Profiles
cards.content: Asos told customers that hackers have detailed profiles of potentially millions of users. The hackers have names addresses phone numbers emails customer numbers and dates of birth. They also have search data like "reclaimed vintage" and "Asos petite". Asos said no bank details or passwords were stolen but customers are warned about potential impersonation scams. The company is still investigating the data breach and will contact customers if more information is needed.

cards.title: Chrysler Building Gets $235 Million Makeover
cards.content: The Chrysler Building in Manhattan is getting a major makeover. The 77-storey skyscraper will have its Art Deco crown polished and its facade restored. The building's 61st floor which has giant eagle gargoyles will also get an upscale lounge. The renovation will cost $235 million and is being led by developer Tishman Speyer. The company plans to use most of the building for office space which is in high demand in the area.
